# Output template

The shape of the profile written to the target file. Keep the two marker lines exactly as shown, since `voice-tune` and `voice-check` find the profile by them. Everything between the markers is yours to adapt: drop any section the person had no view on, and rename or merge sections if that suits their preferences better.

Text in square brackets is guidance for you and must not appear in the output.

```markdown
<!-- voice-profile:start -->
# Writing style

These rules apply to everything you write for me: [the scope they chose, as a short list]. [Any standing exception, in one sentence.]

## My voice

[Three or four sentences of plain prose describing how this person sounds when they write: their register, their rhythm, how direct they are, and what makes them recognisable. Written in the first person, in their voice.]

## Language

[Spelling variant with a few example words, and the code exception if they write code.]
[Contractions, Oxford comma, active or passive, and anything else they settled.]

## Punctuation

[Em dashes: the rule, and what to use instead.]
[En dashes and hyphens.]
[Semicolons, exclamation marks, ellipses, parentheses, quote marks: only the ones they had a view on.]
[Emoji.]

## Tone

[Formality, directness, hedging, warmth, humour. One line each, with a reason where it helps.]
[Register differences, if any: a line each for email, chat, and documents.]

## Words and patterns to avoid

[Banned words, grouped on a few lines.]
[Banned phrases, openers, and closers.]
[Banned sentence patterns, each with a short example so the pattern is recognisable.]
[When one of these would have appeared, restructure the sentence. Don't swap in the nearest synonym.]
[Exceptions: technical terms and direct quotes.]

## Structure

[Prose versus lists, headers, bold, length, how to open, how to end.]

## How I sound

These show rhythm and tone. Don't reuse the phrases.

[Three to six short example sentences the person approved, each on its own line as a quote.]

## Final check

[One or two sentences listing what to scan for before presenting any written output, drawn from their strictest rules.]
<!-- voice-profile:end -->
```

Before showing the profile to the person, check it against itself. It must obey every rule it states, since a future reader will imitate how it's written as much as what it says.
